title: Dynamic computational phenotyping of human cognition
authors: Schurr, Reznik, Hillman, Bhui, et al.
why: Repeated measurement reveals meaningful differences in parameter stability and systematic temporal change—a strong bridge across computational psychiatry, individual differences, and decision science.

title: Disentangling sources of variability in decision-making
why: A shared vocabulary for latent states, evidence accumulation, neural dynamics, and psychiatric phenotypes.

title: Compulsivity is linked to suboptimal choice variability but unaltered reinforcement learning under uncertainty
why: A clean computational-psychiatry example that separates variability in learning from variability in choice.

title: Schemas, reinforcement learning and the medial prefrontal cortex
why: An integrative treatment of schemas, latent states, reinforcement learning, memory, and medial prefrontal function.

title: A neural mechanism for conserved value computations integrating information and rewards
why: A cross-species account of information value, reward, uncertainty, exploration, and lateral habenula.

title: Distributional reinforcement learning in prefrontal cortex
why: An entry point into richer representations of outcome distributions, risk-sensitive behavior, and individual differences.

title: Humans adaptively deploy forward and backward prediction
why: A discussion starter for model-based cognition, representation, planning, and when different computational strategies are rational.

title: Artificial neural networks for model identification and parameter estimation in computational cognitive models
why: A practical anchor for neural model identification, parameter estimation, calibration, recovery, generalization, and failure modes.

title: Flexible and efficient simulation-based inference for models of decision-making
why: Directly relevant background for a hands-on neural and simulation-based inference workshop.

title: Methods and considerations for estimating parameters in biophysically detailed neural models with simulation based inference
why: Useful for diagnostics, identifiability, posterior uniqueness, and the broader logic of simulation-based inference.

title: Computational complexity drives sustained deliberation
why: How formal properties of a decision problem shape effortful deliberation and behavior.

title: Goal commitment is supported by vmPFC through selective attention
why: A neuroimaging-focused discussion of valuation, attention, and goal-directed behavior.

title: Orthogonal neural encoding of targets and distractors supports multivariate cognitive control
why: Connects decision-making with control, representational geometry, and multivariate fMRI.

title: Using games to understand the mind
why: A perspective on richer tasks, ecological validity, large-scale behavioral data, and new experimental paradigms.
